scenes.heading: Substitution and Expanding
scenes.narration: Welcome to part two of our algebra series. Today we substitute numbers into expressions, and we use the distributive law to expand brackets.

scenes.heading: Substitution
bullets: Replace each variable with its value
Put the value in brackets, especially a negative number
Then follow the order of operations
scenes.narration: To substitute, replace each variable with its value. Always put the value in brackets, especially when it is a negative number. Then work it out using the order of operations: brackets, exponents, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.

scenes.heading: Example 1: Substitute x = 3
scenes.narration: Find the value of two x squared, minus five x, plus one, when x is three. Replace x with three in brackets. Square first: three squared is nine, so we get two times nine, minus fifteen, plus one. That is eighteen minus fifteen plus one, which equals four.

scenes.heading: Example 2: Substitute a = -2 and b = 4
scenes.narration: Now find three a minus a b, when a is negative two and b is four. Substitute: three times negative two, minus negative two times four. Three times negative two is negative six. Negative two times four is negative eight. Minus negative eight becomes plus eight. So negative six plus eight equals two.

scenes.heading: The distributive law
bullets: Multiply the term outside by every term inside
scenes.narration: The distributive law says a times, b plus c, equals a b plus a c. Multiply the term outside the bracket by every term inside. Watch the signs: negative two times, x minus three, equals negative two x, plus six, because negative times negative is positive.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Expand
scenes.narration: Expand three times, two x minus five. Three times two x is six x. Three times negative five is negative fifteen. So the answer is six x minus fifteen.

scenes.heading: Example 4: Expand and simplify
scenes.narration: Expand and simplify two x times, x plus four, minus three times, x minus one. Two x times x is two x squared, and two x times four is eight x. Negative three times x is negative three x, and negative three times negative one is plus three. Now add the like terms: eight x minus three x is five x. The answer is two x squared, plus five x, plus three.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: Always use brackets when you substitute
The sign in front of the bracket is multiplied in too
scenes.narration: Remember: always use brackets when you substitute. The sign in front of a bracket is multiplied in too. And after expanding, always simplify the like terms.

activity.title: Substitution and expanding
activity.instructions: Answer all the questions and show your working.
